pride_data.title: The structure and symmetry of the Radial Spoke protein complex in Chlamydomonas flagella
pride_data.projectDescription: Chemical cross-linking coupled to mass spectrometry was used to study the organization of the Radial Spoke protein complex from Chlamydomonas. Experiments were performed by on-bead cross-linking of the immobilized complex with the amine-reactive cross-linking reagent disuccinimidyl suberate (DSS).
pride_data.sampleProcessingProtocol: Chemical cross-linking was performed following previously described procedures (Herzog et al., Science, 2012; Leitner et al., Nat. Protoc., 2014). Samples were digested using endoproteinase Lys-C followed by trypsin. Digests were fractionated by size-exclusion chromatography and SEC fractions were analyzed by data-dependent LC-MS/MS on a Thermo Orbitrap Fusion Lumos system.  Additional experimental details are provided in the accompanying publication.
pride_data.dataProcessingProtocol: MS/MS spectra were searched using xQuest (Walzthoeni et al., Nat. Methods, 2012), version 2.1.4, against the sequences of the complex subunits, co-purified proteins and contaminants.   Additional search/filter settings were as follows: Enzyme = trypsin, maximum number of missed cleavages = 2, MS mass tolerance = 3 ppm, MS/MS mass tolerance = 0.2 Da for “common”-type fragment ions and 0.3 Da for “xlink”-type fragment ions. The original scoring scheme of xQuest (Rinner et al., Nat. Methods, 2008) was used.
keywords: Chemical cross-linking; dss; structural proteomics; radial spoke complex
